info.name: TaskFlow API
info.description:
Tests for the TaskFlow API against the seeded development database (see docs/DATABASE.md).

1. Start PostgreSQL (`docker compose up -d`) and the API (`dotnet run --launch-profile https` in src/TaskFlow.API).
2. Check `baseUrl` in the collection variables (default https://localhost:7103).
3. Run the whole collection in order with the Collection Runner: later requests use tokens and ids saved by earlier ones.

All seeded accounts use the password in the `password` variable. Re-runnable: each run registers and then deletes its own user; the tasks it creates remain until you reset the database.

item.name: 3. Tasks
item.description: Only POST /api/tasks exists so far. Created tasks stay in the database (there is no delete endpoint); reset with `dotnet run -- --Seed:ResetDatabase=true`.

item.name: Manager creates a task assigned to Sam

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Postman: review API collection",
  "description": "Created by the Postman collection",
  "priority": "High",
  "dueDate": "{{dueDate}}",
  "assignedToId": "44444444-4444-4444-4444-444444444444"
}

exec: pm.test("Starts as Todo with the requested priority", () => { pm.expect(task.status).to.eql("Todo"); pm.expect(task.priority).to.eql("High"); });
pm.test("New task has no comments and no updatedAt", () => { pm.expect(task.commentsCount).to.eql(0); pm.expect(task.updatedAt).to.eql(null); });

item.name: User creates an unassigned task, spoofing createdById

request.description: The body claims the Admin created it; the server must ignore that and use the caller from the token.

exec: pm.test("Creator is the caller, not the id in the body", () => pm.expect(task.createdById).to.eql("33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333"));
